Classic spreads evenly. Supersaw uses a centre voice plus detuned sides. Octaves, Power and Minor stack intervals. JP Super follows the measured JP-8000 curves: narrow detune until near the top, Blend trades the centre against the sides, and a high-pass at the note removes low rumble. Best with 7 voices.
Number of stacked voices per note. Drag a modulator onto it.
Unison detune. The curve is slow at first and steep at the end. Drag a modulator onto it.
Blend only works in the Supersaw style. Set Style to Supersaw to use it.
Stereo spread of the unison voices. Drag a modulator onto it.
Down one octave (12 semitones). Tip: hold Ctrl, Cmd or Alt while dragging or scrolling the Semi knob to do the same.

Pitch shift in semitones, 0 in the centre, up to 4 octaves up or down. The < and > buttons next to it move by a whole octave; Ctrl, Cmd or Alt while dragging or scrolling the knob does the same. Drag a modulator onto it.
Up one octave (12 semitones). Tip: hold Ctrl, Cmd or Alt while dragging or scrolling the Semi knob to do the same.
Fine tune in cents. Drag a modulator onto it.

Start phase. Drag a modulator onto it.
Random start phase. 0 gives the same attack every note. Drag a modulator onto it.
Pitch dive at note start. The note starts this far off and falls into tune. Used for hoover sounds. Drag a modulator onto it.
How long the dive takes. Drag a modulator onto it.

Analog life for this oscillator. Each voice and unison voice gets a tiny fixed pitch offset plus a slow drift, like a real analog poly; filter cutoff and envelope times of the voice get a small spread too (the highest Analog of the playing oscillators sets that part). Chords and unison breathe and sound wider and warmer. At 100%: about 5 cents fixed, 3 cents drift, 3% cutoff, 5% envelope times. 0% is exact and digital. Drag a modulator onto it.
Which envelope shapes the volume of OSC A. Env 1 is the main amp envelope. Pick another to give this source its own attack and tail, then edit it in the envelope bank.

items.txt: Each track can go to Master, to an FX bus, or into a later track (B, C or Sub+Noise), so you can build chains of tracks. Sends feed FX 1 and FX 2, which each have their own effect chain on the FX page. FX 1 can also feed FX 2. FX Out is one fader for all effect returns together, then it goes to Master. Send levels are post-fader.
Oscillators go to a track with the To menu on the Sound page, and to filters with Route.
Meters show level in dB with a peak marker: blue is low, purple is hot, pink from -1 dB up is close to clipping.
